signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Divergence
signals.text: USD outperforms the G10 complex with a 1W average of +0.900% across 9 pairs, while NOK lags at -1.907% across 2 pairs, establishing a 2.807% bilateral spread. Fed's Bowman reaffirmed hawkish policy vigilance, highlighting persistent inflation and firming labor conditions that keep US rates restrictive. The policy backdrop features the Fed at 4.00% against Norges Bank at 4.50%, but front-end momentum has shifted as US 2Y yields trade at 4.510% alongside a bear-steepening curve. USD/NOK trades at 9.506, printing a wide-range bullish engulfing bar that cleared the SMA20 (9.354), SMA50 (9.406), and SMA200 (9.488) moving average stack. Spot strength reflects broad dollar demand following stronger US price pressures, pushing the pair to fresh swing highs despite nominal carry favoring NOK. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, supported by widening G10 performance divergence and hawkish Fed repricing. Catalyst: Norges Bank Financial Stability Report on 11 Nov. Risk: Break back below the SMA200 at 9.488 invalidating the technical breakout.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Advantage vs Downside Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.74, holding above its SMA20 (157.95), SMA50 (157.24), and SMA200 (158.67) cluster after clearing local resistance at 158.47. A 266bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.89% vs TONA 1.23%) anchors structural demand, while 160.00 remains the key watch level that has previously triggered verbal warnings. However, the options market reflects asymmetric hedging demand, with the 1-month 25-delta risk reversal printing at -1.99, indicating severe put skew against base strength. Realized volatility sits at 4.9% against an implied volatility of 6.6%, generating a +1.7% vol risk premium. While CFTC positioning shows JPY leveraged funds net short -21,213 contracts at the 92nd percentile of their 52-week range, options participants are paying a substantial premium for downside protection as spot tests multi-month highs. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while spot holds above 158.00. Catalyst: BoJ L Money Stock release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Sharp compression in the 266bp OIS spread or formal intervention rhetoric forcing an unwind through the SMA50 at 157.24.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Downtrend vs Positive Carry Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6869, extending below its falling SMA20 (0.6984), SMA50 (0.7037), and SMA200 (0.7058) in an established technical downtrend. Intraday price action broke the horizontal support zone near 0.6905, leaving spot extended 2.43 ATR below its 20-day moving average. The sharp selloff runs counter to underlying cash carry, where RBA at 4.85% vs Fed at 4.00% yields an 85bp nominal advantage (and a 96bp OIS carry premium via AONIA 4.85% vs SOFR 3.89%). Leveraged funds hold +43,532 net long contracts (46th percentile), yet retail traders have built a 70% net-long posture, attempting to catch falling knives. BEER valuation models flag AUD/USD as undervalued at z = -2.40σ, but technical momentum remains firmly negative following the US inflation data release. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, trend continuation below broken support at 0.6905. Catalyst: Fed Vice Chair Barr speech on 11 Nov. Risk: Daily close back above 0.6905 support-turned-resistance signaling mean reversion toward the SMA20.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short at Structural Range Lows
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1167, remaining range-bound within a tight 20-session box below its SMA20 (1.1197), SMA50 (1.1330), and SMA200 (1.1538). The macro backdrop heavily favors the dollar, backed by a 135bp rate spread (Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65%) and a 145bp OIS advantage (SOFR 3.89% vs €STR 2.44%). However, CFTC positioning highlights stretched institutional bearishness: leveraged funds sit net short -104,030 contracts, corresponding to the 2nd percentile of the 52-week range and z = -1.80σ. Furthermore, retail traders are 84% long, highlighting an extreme directional divergence against institutional flow. Options pricing shows neutral sentiment with 25-delta risk reversals at -0.18 and a modest vol risk premium of +1.1% (IV 5.8% vs HV30 4.7%), suggesting institutional participants are reluctant to chase downside momentum at current levels. Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD, constrained by crowded speculative short positioning. Catalyst: Germany CPI release on 11 Nov at 07:00 UTC. Risk: Clean break below 1.1100 triggering a fresh wave of momentum selling.
